source_note: baseline.py:25-27 says only 'a convention, not a cited rule'; no methods reason is given. STRATIFICATION_OPTIMISM.md:128-129 and :149 and RECIPES_AND_TUNING.md:1355 reuse MIN_GAIN but state it as '0.01 nats', that is, they reason only for log loss. No document justifies 0.01 for MSE in squared outcome units, the RPS or Brier(t). The code applies it to PRIMARY[task] unscaled (metrics.py:89, 216, 315: raw-scale MSE; baseline.py:97 tolerance = max(MIN_GAIN, t*se)).
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/test_seal.py::test_a_gain_inside_the_tolerance_is_no_better_than_the_baseline (checks only that tolerance == MIN_GAIN in the verdict mechanics, not that 0.01 is a meaningful gain on any scale)
note: The statement is faithful: the app applies one unscaled threshold to every task's primary and tells users that a smaller gain is 'too little to matter'. On raw-scale MSE that threshold depends on the outcome's units. It is negligible for an outcome in mg/dL, and it is a large share of variance for an outcome on a 0-1 scale, so the convention is not coherent for regression. Scale it (for example as a share of the baseline MSE, i.e. an R² gain of 0.01) or soften the wording. The verdict 'better' also requires the interval to clear zero (tolerance = max(0.01, half-width)).

corrected_statement: For tuning XGBoost under prediction at an effective size of at least 300, the app searches a box it calls 'conventions, narrowed' from Probst, Boulesteix & Bischl 2019. The box is: learning rate [0.01, 0.3] (log); depth [2, 10]; least child weight [1, 64] rows-equivalent (log), times the mean hessian at the base score; row share [0.5, 1]; column share [0.3, 1]; λ [1e-3, 100] (log); rounds [25, 1,000] (log integer), searched only when early stopping is off (up to 2,000 rounds, patience 50, otherwise). α = 0, the tree booster and hist are fixed, and XGBoost's defaults are always a candidate. The app does not claim the box contains the best settings.
source_note: I verified Probst, Boulesteix & Bischl (JMLR 2019, arXiv 1802.09596v3 HTML). Table 1 has λ 2^[-10,10] and min_child_weight 2^[0,7], as cited, but these are the random-search sampling bounds, not a recommended box. Table 3 ('tuning space', the 0.05-0.95 quantiles of the best values) gives eta 0.002-0.355, max_depth 5.6-14, min_child_weight 1.295-6.984, subsample 0.545-0.958, colsample_bytree 0.419-0.864, lambda 0.008-29.755, nrounds 920.7-4550.95 and alpha 0.002-6.105. The app's box leaves out depth 11-14, eta below 0.01 and, without early stopping, rounds above 1,000, which is most of Probst's well-performing round counts. Probst's child weight is in raw hessian units; the app's is rows-equivalent times the mean hessian. RECIPES_AND_TUNING.md §4.1 (lines 754-764) gives the table and says only 'The ranges are conventions, narrowed from the sources above ... the prediction reviewer's packet asks for them to be checked'. That is a decision, not a methods reason for the narrowing.
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/test_xgboost_family.py::test_the_standard_settings_are_xgboosts_own_defaults (pins the defaults; no test checks that the box contains well-performing settings)
note: The code matches the stated box and fixed settings exactly (xgboost_family.py:482-512). 'Contains the well-performing settings' overstates the app's own wording and conflicts with Probst's Table 3 for depth, and for rounds without early stopping. Present the box as a narrowed convention, and flag depth up to 10 and rounds up to 1,000 for the prediction reviewer's packet. The ruled small-sample standard (RECIPES §4.6) is not in xgboost_family.py, but it applies only below 300, outside this regime.

source_note: I verified Sisk, Sperrin, Peek, van Smeden & Martin, Stat Methods Med Res 2023;32(8):1461-77 (PMID 37105540; abstract from Europe PMC). It says: 'With complete data available at deployment ... the outcome should be used to impute development data when using multiple imputation ... When missingness is allowed at deployment, omitting the outcome from the imputation model at the development was preferred.' It also found MI and regression imputation 'comparable', and 'the performance ... must be evaluated on a study-by-study basis'. So Sisk supports omitting the outcome when new rows can have blanks. It does not make MI with the outcome 'invalid' under prediction in general: with complete data at deployment it recommends that MI. BLUEPRINT.md §12 ruling 4 (line 474) gives a methods reason ('so the fitted pipeline can be deployed') and cites Moons 2006, Sterne 2009 and Sisk 2023.
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_wp7_missing_data.py::test_1_multiple_imputation_with_the_outcome_is_refused_under_prediction (pins the refusal code and its exits; it would pass whether or not MI with the outcome harms prediction)
note: The code (decisions.py:4815-4843) refuses MI whenever purpose != 'inference', so also when no purpose is set. The refusal text matches the claim. The leakage half (a held-out row's outcome filling its own predictors) holds for MI over the whole table before splitting. It does not rule out MI with the outcome fitted in-fold on the training rows only, which Sisk studies and which the app does not offer. Reword as the app's deployment-driven rule: new rows can arrive with blanks and no outcome, and Sisk et al. found omitting the outcome preferred in that case. Do not call MI with the outcome invalid in general.

source_note: No basis is cited in percent_energy.py or its docstring. The 0-100 bound follows from the definition: a share of total energy cannot be negative or exceed 100%. The rule that values all at or below 1 must be fractions is a data-sanity heuristic with no stated source.
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_wp12a_percent_energy.py::test_b24_shares_are_never_moved_in_kcal_and_fractions_are_refused (divides synthetic percentages by 100 and checks the ValueError; it would not fail if a genuine percent column with every value <= 1 existed)
note: The code matches the claim (percent_energy.py:52-64: refused if min < 0, max > 100, or max <= 1; the name gate is PERCENT_SUFFIX plus nutrient_role, whose roles include protein, carbohydrate, fat, alcohol and fiber). The 0-100 half is definitional. The <= 1 half is a heuristic stated to the user as fact ('it holds fractions'). It would wrongly refuse a real percent-of-energy column for a minor source, such as alcohol in a light-drinking sample, fiber, or a trans-fat share. The ValueError offers no exit or user override. Reword as 'reads as fractions' and add a way to confirm the values are percentages.

corrected_statement: Complete-case analysis gives (approximately) unbiased regression coefficients when whether a value is missing does not depend on the outcome given the predictors. That is a sufficient condition, not a necessary one. For logistic-regression odds ratios, missingness that depends on the outcome alone (not on the incomplete covariate) also leaves them unbiased; only the intercept is biased.
source_note: I verified White & Carlin, Stat Med 2010;29:2920-31 (PMID 20842622, Europe PMC abstract). It says 'when missingness is independent of the outcome given the covariates, CC has negligible bias', which is the sufficient direction only. It does not say 'only if'. Groenwold et al., CMAJ 2012;184:1265 (PMID 22371511) is real; Europe PMC has no abstract, and its subject is the missing-indicator method; I could not verify its complete-case wording. The known exception to necessity, outcome-dependent selection in logistic regression leaving the odds ratios unbiased (case-control logic; Bartlett, Harel & Carpenter, Am J Epidemiol 2015), contradicts 'only if' in the claim's stated regime (linear, logistic, Cox).
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_wp7_missing_data.py::test_1_multiple_imputation_is_unbiased_and_its_intervals_cover (a known-truth simulation, 400 x 1,000 rows. It checks the sufficient direction in one linear scenario, missingness depending on the exposure, with complete cases |bias| < 0.01. Nothing tests necessity or a logistic/Cox model)
note: The app asserts both directions. The option label says 'Sound if ...' (missing.py:139), while COMPLETE_CASE_ASSUMPTION (missing.py:75-77) and row_loss_concern (missing.py:1763-1764) say 'only if' / 'estimate without bias only if'. The rendered label nests the two ('Sound if complete cases give unbiased coefficients only if ...'), which reads garbled. The grade covers the sufficient half, which is sourced and simulation-checked in one linear case. The 'only if' half is unsupported by the cited sources and false for logistic odds ratios. Reword to 'if', and add the logistic exception or scope the claim to linear models.

source_note: I verified Li & Redden, Stat Med 2015;34:281-96 (PMID 25345738; full text PMC4268228). It says 'In the case of two intervention arms, the degrees of freedom can be approximated as K − 2 ... In our simulations, K − 2 degrees of freedom approximation is used', and the KC correction with t holds nominal size down to 10 clusters for binary outcomes. Its Discussion says: 'we do not consider covariates other than the treatment ... The addition of covariates will change the variance estimation and the degrees of freedom'. So K − 2 is sourced, for two arms, no covariates and binary outcomes. Subtracting each cluster-level covariate (and more arm terms) is the app's own extension, not stated by Li & Redden. It is a common between-cluster df convention, but no source for it is cited here.
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_e2_trials.py::test_gee_intervals_are_t_on_the_clusters_less_the_cluster_level_terms (asserts df == 12 − 3 and the interval string for one fixture: the rule's application, not its calibration. No type-I-error or coverage simulation of the df rule was found)
note: The code matches: trials.py:1365-1366 df = K − len(cluster_level_columns), with cluster_level_columns at 1186-1196 counting every column constant within clusters (intercept, arm columns, cluster-level covariates). It is passed to _gee and named in the interval line. The base case (K − 2) is sourced. The cluster-level-covariate extension and its use for numeric outcomes under GEE go beyond Li & Redden's regime and should be labeled a convention or given a source. The same df is also computed, and refused when < 1, for the mixed-model path, which then uses Kenward-Roger.

corrected_statement: When the Newton fit does not converge, which includes any standardized coefficient running past 20 (|β_j|·SD(x_j) > 20, DIVERGED), the app reads the Cox partial likelihood as having no finite maximum (monotone likelihood). It names the runaway columns (or every column, if none passed 20), calls the hazard ratio infinite, and reports no interval or p-value, with 'leave it out or merge its rare levels' as the exit. Monotone likelihood arises when a covariate orders the risk sets perfectly at every event time; a group with no events is the usual case. A group in which every row has the event does not by itself produce it, and non-convergence for other reasons gets the same message.
source_note: None is cited. survival.py:59 says only 'a log hazard ratio of 20 per SD is an infinite one', a convention. The phenomenon is real: Heinze & Schemper, Biometrics 2001;57:114-19 (PMID 11252585, abstract verified) define monotone likelihood as 'the likelihood converges to a finite value while at least one parameter estimate diverges'. They also give a remedy, Firth-penalized estimates with profile-penalized-likelihood intervals, which shows that an interval and a test can be reported. The app does not cite this.
test_judged: none found: no test in turbotab/core/tests exercises the non-convergence refusal of cox_table or the survey Cox table (searched 'no maximum', 'DIVERGED', 'monotone', and the cox_fit / cox_table callers)
note: The code is at survival.py:247-296 (converged = decrement < tol and no |β_z| > 20) and survival.py:472-481 and 573-581 (the refusal). The trigger is any non-convergence; the 20-SD rule only selects the columns named. The parenthetical shown to users, 'in one of its groups every row has the event, or none does', misstates the cause: 'every row has the event' is not sufficient, and it is wrong for a continuous covariate. A fit that fails to converge for another reason (ill-conditioning, too few iterations) is told its likelihood has no maximum. Reword, add a test with a known monotone fixture (a group with zero events), and consider the Firth exit (Heinze & Schemper 2001).

source_note: I verified Riley et al., BMJ 2016;353:i3140 (PMC4916924 full text). It says 'Rather than focusing on I2, which might be misleading when the study sample sizes are large, the extent of heterogeneity in model performance is better quantified by a 95% prediction interval', and recommends 'deriving 95% prediction intervals for calibration and discrimination performance in a new cluster' for internal-external validation. The formula μ̂ ± t(k−2)·√(τ̂² + σ̂_μ²) is Higgins, Thompson & Spiegelhalter's (JRSS A 2009). I did not fetch that paper, but metafor's predtype='Riley' implements it and the repo matches it numerically. The k ≥ 3 requirement follows from the t(k−2) df.
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_site_validation.py::test_reml_with_hksj_and_the_riley_interval_match_metafor (an independent R metafor reference, rel 1e-8, for the PI bounds, τ², I², Q and the HKSJ CI on both scales; it certifies the computation, not the reporting preference over I²)
note: The code matches: site_validation.py:244-253 computes the PI for k >= 3 (t(k−2), REML τ² and the non-HKSJ σ̂_μ, as metafor's Riley PI does); _says (474-487) states the PI before I²; MIN_SITES = 3 refuses fewer sites (line 364). The formula is certified against metafor. The preference for the PI over I² is a reporting judgment sourced to Riley 2016; nothing tests it, and no test is needed. Note that the user-facing sentence gives the PI and I² without citing Riley; the methods sentence cites Higgins et al.

source_note: BLUEPRINT.md §14.3 (lines 613-640) is an internal ruling with a reason: 'A kind is settled by its values only when it declares its plausible alternatives and a value test that rejects each of them ... A kind without such a test is settled only by the user or the codebook'. Its fourth-gate list names 'a label count read as free text (country of birth has 70)'. The design-role alternatives come from the KIND_RULES declarations (readings.py:1121-1128), not from a separate document. No external literature is involved; this is an epistemic and design rule, not a statistical claim.
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_discriminate.py::test_a6_a_category_with_many_labels_is_asked_never_dropped_as_free_text (a known-truth fixture: a 70-label country-of-birth category is not proposed as excluded at high confidence, and each answer is honored). With ::test_b7_a_label_count_settles_no_free_text (asserts KIND_RULES['role:free_text'].test is None), these enforce the policy. They cannot show that no value test could discriminate. No test for role:design was found.
note: The code matches: KIND_RULES role:free_text and role:design declare their alternatives and no value test (test=None), and readings.by_values raises if a consumer tries to settle either by values (readings.py:400-407). Design is 'settled by the user's confirmation of the role, and the survey answer'. The claim is a conservative ask-the-user ruling, not a quantitative statement, so presenting it as an ask is appropriate.

corrected_statement: The app reads a column named like an identifier by its values (recognizers.identifier_values). Fewer than 3 distinct values, or at most 10 repeating values that are all digit-free words, read as a category's labels ('never'). The column is then proposed as a predictor at low confidence, 'kept as a predictor until you say otherwise'; it is not refused. One value per row, or more than 10 repeating coded values (with digits), reads as a unit structure. 3-10 repeating coded values, or more than 10 repeating word values, are 'few': asked, never high. Clustering intervals by fewer than the cluster floor is refused separately, by inference.floor_refusal.
source_note: BLUEPRINT.md §14 rule 1 (line 547) says 'An identifier has at least 3 distinct values and a unit structure', as the condition for HIGH confidence, not as a rule that fewer values are never units. The reason it gives is the gate anecdote (a case-control `participant` yes/no clustered intervals into no interval). FEW_UNITS = 10 is tied to CATEGORY_LEVELS in a code comment (recognizers.py:1412-1425); it is a convention, not a methods source. The rule that word labels without digits are not unit codes is a judgment in a code comment ('a unit's codes almost always carry digits'). This is a decision with an anecdotal rationale, not a methods reason.
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_recognition_leash.py::test_a2_the_case_control_inference_never_clusters_by_a_category (a real-server, known-truth fixture: no interval clusters by the 0/1 `patient`, the Self/Proxy `respondent`, etc. It does not exercise the 3-10 boundary, the more-than-10 word case or a pseudonym-coded small study)
note: The code is recognizers.py:1440-1467, consumed at stages/rows.py:507-511 (a 'never' verdict gives a predictor at low confidence, with the user able to override). The claim overstates in three ways. 'More than 10 repeating values is a unit structure' holds only for coded values; word values above 10 are 'few'. The app keeps the column as an overridable predictor rather than refusing it. 'Clustering by it is invalid' is not something the recognizer asserts; the interval floor (FEW_CLUSTERS = 30) separately refuses too few clusters. The digit-free-word rule would misread a small study whose participants are coded by names. The low-confidence proposal and its visible reason mitigate this.

source_note: I verified Broadhurst et al., Metabolomics 2018;14:72 (PMC5960010 full text). It defines D-ratio_i = s_qc / s_sample × 100% (Eq. 3), approximately σ_tech / √(σ_bio² + σ_tech²) (Eq. 5; 100% means no biological information), and says 'it is recommended that the acceptance criterion for D-ratio is set to, at most, < 50% (preferably much lower)'. The repo's quote drops 'recommended' and '(preferably much lower)', but the substance matches. Broadhurst also advises log-transforming non-Gaussian data before computing the D-ratio, or using a MAD version (Eq. 4). The app computes SDs on the corrected, unlogged scale: DRatioFilter is the first adjust step, before 'log', in pipeline.py:76 and 634-639. The in-fold placement is the app's own leakage rule, consistent with its method contract (training-fold scope).
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/test_heldout_guarantee.py (the 'd_ratio_filter' entry checks that the in-fold step is never moved by held-out rows; no test checks the 50% threshold or the removal against an independent D-ratio computation)
note: The code matches: D_RATIO_MAX = 0.50 (qc_drift.py:59); DRatioFilter drops features with not (ratio < 0.5) (qc_drift.py:446-470); the QC SD is frozen from the reference rows and the study SD comes from the fitting rows (ddof = 1); a feature with no QC SD is kept. It is an option variant (qc_rlsc_*_dratio), not a default. The methods sentence (line 735-737) matches what the user sees. Two caveats: Broadhurst calls 50% an upper bound ('preferably much lower'), and the app does not log-transform or use the MAD version for skewed features.

source_note: I verified Ambroise & McLachlan, PNAS 2002;99:6562-6 (PMC124442 full text). With class labels randomly permuted (no information) and genes selected by RFE outside the CV, 'we can form an SVM rule that has not only an average zero AE but also an average CV1IE error close to zero for a subset of 128 genes'; 10-fold CV or .632+ external to selection corrects it. This is the near-zero-error-without-signal claim, in a p >> n regime. The internal packs exist and say this: CLINICAL_SURVEY_PACK.md §A5.5 (lines 634-638: 'Internal validation must resample the entire modeling pipeline ... [SETTLED that the full pipeline must be inside the loop]') and GENOMICS_PACK.md lines 406-411. That unsupervised steps (scaling, PCA, imputation) also belong in-fold rests on the cited Hornung 2015 and Moscovich & Rosset 2022, which show unsupervised preprocessing can bias CV. I did not fetch these.
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_rt5a_t1_nested_tuning.py::test_t1_flat_tuning_is_optimistic_and_nested_tuning_is_not (a known-truth simulation scored against 20,000 fresh rows: flat tuning is optimistic and nested tuning is not. It covers the tuning component only, is slow and scheduled, and was not run here). For selection: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_explore_3_selection.py::test_3_selection_outside_the_resampling_is_refused_with_the_exit_run_it_in_fold only pins the refusal, and no null-data test shows the near-zero error. turbotab/core/tests/test_heldout_guarantee.py checks the app's implementation (held-out rows never move a learned step), not the principle.
note: The teaching text (content.py:86-90, 471-475, 1009-1013, 1132-1136, 1363-1367) matches the claim and carries a SETTLED badge with its pack source. Grade 'sourced': the principle is established in the literature, and the repo certifies by known-truth simulation only the tuning component (T1). It is consistent with WHAT_EXPLORATION row 1, which lets inference fit outcome-free steps on all rows; this is a prediction-only rule.

corrected_statement: The app's teaching card and censored-values finding say that a TNTC count is right-censored above the countable range (15-300 colonies per plate in FDA BAM ch. 3, January 2026 edition), not missing, and that QNS or a hemolyzed specimen is a measurement failure to treat as missing. The app has no censored handling for TNTC. The censored-values finding has no repair, and the only repair offered for such a text column ('Read as numbers', repairs.py:918-944) sets TNTC cells blank, i.e. missing, along with every other non-number.
source_note: I verified FDA BAM ch. 3 (Aerobic Plate Count), January 2026 edition PDF (fda.gov/media/191248). The revision history reads 'March 2025: The suitable colony counting range updated from 25-250 to 15-300 per plate'. The text says 'Maximum likelihood (ML) is used to estimate the Poisson mean APC (CFU/ml) using the plates for which exact counts are available and the too numerous to count (TNTC) plates', and 'If a count of visible colonies is available, then this is the lower bound'. That supports TNTC as a censored lower bound, for aerobic plate counts in food microbiology. The app applies it under the clinical lens: the sample's TNTC column is `wbc`, where TNTC usually means cells per high-power field in urine microscopy. There the BAM's 15-300 colonies-per-plate range is the wrong regime, although the censoring logic still holds. The QNS/hemolyzed-as-missing half has no external source beyond CLINICAL_SURVEY_PACK §A1.3, an internal ruling. A hemolyzed specimen often still yields values, flagged, for many analytes.
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_wp15_claims.py::test_4_tntc_is_right_censored_in_the_finding_on_the_sample_labs and ::test_4_tntc_in_the_teaching_and_the_pack (check only that the text says right-censored, 15-300 and the 2026 edition). The legacy test turbotab/test_the_clinical_detectors_reach_an_upload.py::test_tntc_and_qns_are_measurement_failures_and_never_censoring still asserts the opposite (TNTC among measurement failures).
note: The words and the behavior disagree. The teaching (content.py:265-272) and finding_words.py:224-306 say TNTC is censored, not missing. But turbotab/clinical.py:138 still lists 'tntc' in _FAILURE_TOKENS, packs.py:5573 still describes TNTC as a measurement failure, and the only lever, 'Read as numbers', blanks TNTC cells. That is the deletion of the highest values the text warns against. The BAM range is cited for clinical lab columns outside its food plate-count regime. Either implement censored handling (for example a lower-bound value with a censoring indicator) or say plainly that the app does not yet model TNTC as censored, and scope the 15-300 range to plate counts.

corrected_statement: In a ruling for the Predict design (BEATS_PREDICT §17 ruling 4, 2026-10-11, beat D), values filled before the table was made, by an unrecorded method, are to be read as missing and filled again in each training fold at the median, without indicators and without the outcome. The ruling's reason is that their missingness belongs to the upstream process, not the person, and the fill marker does not exist at the moment of use. The engine does not yet serve this: P22, 'a flag linked to its measure; read as missing Recommended', is listed as new work, and BEATS_PREDICT.md:26-28 says 'the engine does not serve them yet: P22-P24'.
source_note: This is an internal ruling (BEATS_PREDICT.md lines 1486-1488) with a stated reason, but the reason is the orchestrator's own. The cited sources support only parts of it. Sisk et al. 2023 (verified under A-117) supports imputing without the outcome when blanks occur at deployment, and finds regression imputation and MI comparable; it does not address re-reading upstream-imputed values as missing, or median fill. TRIPOD+AI item 11 (Collins et al., BMJ 2024;385:e078378, PMC11019967, verified) reads 'Describe how missing data were handled. Provide reasons for omitting any data': a reporting item, with no ruling on provider-imputed values. No source addresses whether indicators are appropriate here.
test_judged: none found: no engine test, because the behavior is unimplemented (no P22 code in turbotab/core; searched 'filled before', 'Read them as missing', 'P22')
note: The claim describes planned behavior. The current engine has no filled-values decision; the captured beat applied it outside the engine (predict-capture/capture.py). The reasoning has a gap the inventory noted. If the upstream fill depended on the person (a cuff failing on large arms), the missingness is informative. If deployment data come through the same upstream pipeline, the fill marker does exist at the moment of use, so dropping indicators is a choice, not a consequence. Implement P22 with a test before the app relies on it, and present the rule as a judgment.

corrected_statement: The understanding-layer design (WHAT_EXPLORATION_MAY_DECIDE §1-2; UNDERSTANDING_LAYER §0 item 5) rules as follows. Outcome-blind views may shape the representation; under inference, steps learned without the outcome may be fit on the full analysis sample. Outcome-using views may, under prediction, only add candidates to a declared search (never prune it), with supervised steps refit in each fold. Under inference they are reported, not acted on, unless a declared selection-aware method carries them. The design says this is enforced when an exploration thread registers. No thread registry exists in turbotab/core yet. Today parts are enforced by individual validators: selection outside the resampling is refused under prediction, and selection under inference is only a labeled sensitivity analysis.
source_note: Ambroise & McLachlan 2002 is verified (PMC124442; see D-017): supervised selection outside CV gives near-zero error on no-information data. Harrell RMS §4.7 (data reduction 'masked to Y'), Gelman & Loken 2013 (forking paths), Belloni, Chernozhukov & Hansen 2014 (post-double-selection) and Baillie 2022 (SAP changes 'well motivated, and well documented') are correctly attributed in the doc's table. I did not fetch them; they are standard works whose content matches the attribution. Together they support the outcome-blind/outcome-using split and the selection-aware-inference requirement. No source states the specific 'add candidates, never prune' rule under prediction. ESL 7.10.2 and Varma & Simon 2006 require supervised steps to be inside the resampling, which permits in-fold pruning. 'Never prune' is the app's stricter convention.
test_judged: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_explore_3_selection.py::test_3_selection_outside_the_resampling_is_refused_with_the_exit_run_it_in_fold and ::test_7_under_inference_selection_is_only_a_labeled_sensitivity_analysis (pin the validators' refusals; there is no test of thread-registration enforcement, because no registry exists)
note: The doc is faithfully summarized. 'Enforced at registration' (UNDERSTANDING_LAYER §0 item 5) describes planned architecture: I searched turbotab/core for a thread registry or outcome-use declaration and found none. The claim is that the app refuses; it currently refuses only through specific validators. The grade covers the sourced principle. 'Add candidates, never prune' should be labeled the app's convention, since in-fold pruning under nested CV is valid by the same sources. Each rule must also be declared before the data judge it and rerun in every resample (§1).
